questions.question: When will an automatic tractor protection valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
When wheels regain traction after a skid.
When air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: What is the best way to know your trailer is starting to skid?

options.text: By seeing it in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: By seeing it in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: The easiest and earliest way to notice a trailer skid is to see the trailer move off-course in your mirrors.

questions.question: Why do combination vehicles need extra space on the road?

options.text: They drive slower than other large vehicles.
They are heavier than other large vehicles.
They need more space to turn and stop than other large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more space to turn and stop than other large vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and need more space to turn and stop than other large vehicles. Managing space properly is important when driving a combination vehicle.

questions.question: What happens when an air supply control is in the "emergency" position?
questions.explanation: In older vehicles, tractor protection controls may use levers instead of knobs. When the air supply control is set to "emergency," the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes apply.

questions.question: How should you brake when using ABS?

options.text: Push the brake pedal harder than normal.
Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
Push the brake pedal more lightly than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
questions.explanation: When using anti-lock brakes (ABS), brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, the air supply control lever should be in what position?
questions.explanation: In older vehicles, tractor protection controls may use levers instead of knobs. The air supply control should be in the "normal" position when pulling a trailer.

questions.question: How should you check that air reaches all trailers before driving?

options.text: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Close the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Disconnect air supply lines and listen for escaping air.
Roll each trailer down a hill and test the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that air reaches all trailers. Let air pressure build, send air to both emergency and service lines, and open the shut-off valves on the last trailer's rear. If air escapes from these valves, air is flowing to the entire combination.

questions.question: Before backing under a trailer to couple it, the trailer brakes should be:
questions.explanation: Safe coupling and uncoupling of trailers is critical for operating a combination vehicle safely. Before backing your tractor under the trailer, make sure the trailer brakes are locked.

questions.question: Which vehicle is most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to flip over from the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: What can the "crack-the-whip" effect cause?
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can cause trailers to flip over. The last trailer in a combination is most at risk. Drivers should understand this movement in their vehicle and drive carefully.

questions.question: How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: Keeping cargo low can:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you turn too quickly. Keep cargo low and close to the ground to lower the vehicle's center of gravity and prevent rollovers.

questions.question: Operating combination vehicles usually requires ____ operating single vehicles.

options.text: About the same level of skill as

questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single vehicles. They require more driving skill to operate safely.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.
To test the lights on the trailer.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes.

questions.question: Using the trailer hand valve while driving:
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. It can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: Pushing in the trailer air supply control will:
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
The rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, open all shut-off valves except the last ones on the rear trailer. This ensures air reaches all brake systems and does not escape from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: When traveling under 40 mph, maintain at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Large vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, the tractor should be positioned:

options.text: Directly in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer when backing up to couple. Backing at an angle could move the trailer and break the landing gear.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a major leak
A valve that prevents the truck from being stolen
A valve that prevents the driver from going too fast
A valve that prevents the trailer from being accidentally released

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a major leak
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.
